script.opening_words:
Renee and Desmond are sitting at their
kitchen table on a Tuesday night and
there's an envelope between them that
neither one wants to open. It isn't a
bill. It's from their mortgage serer and
the subject line reads annual escrow
account disclosure statement, which is
the most boring arrangement of words in
the English language and also the reason
they're about to have the worst
conversation of their marriage. Desmond
opens it. Their payment just went up $37
a month. Not their rent, not an
adjus
script.ending_words:
trained to ask one
question when we buy a house, which is
whether we can afford the payment. It's
the wrong question because there's an
assumption buried inside it, which is
that the payment is a fixed object
sitting still. The better question is
whether you can afford this payment when
it's 15% higher in a year you didn't
plan for a reason that has nothing to do
with you because that year is coming. It
comes for almost everybody. Your rate is
locked in. Nothing else is. And the only
real difference between the people it
wrecks and the people it merely
irritates is whether they saw it coming.
